description: The complete normalization allowlist. The differ applies these rules, and only these rules, to both the Go and the Rust side before comparing. Every rule cites the Go source of a nondeterminism: Go itself produces different values for the same input, so no exact Go-vs-Rust comparison is possible there. A new rule must cite a Go nondeterminism source, must turn a Go-vs-Go (A/A) self-test diff into zero, and must never hide a Go-vs-Rust difference. Everything not listed here is a mismatch, including everything in not_normalized.

actions.sort: Sort the array at target by the listed keys (stable, ascending, lexical on the JSON text of each key) before comparing.
actions.drop: Remove the member at target on both sides.
actions.key_set: Compare only the set of member names of the object at target, not the values.
actions.shape: Compare only presence and JSON type (and, for strings, the pattern) of the value at target.
actions.uuid_placeholder: Replace each UUID value at target with <uuid#n>, numbered by first appearance after all sort rules ran, so equal UUIDs stay equal and cross-references are still checked.
actions.count_only: Compare only the count member of a timing value (histogram _count, observation count); ignore sum and buckets.
actions.ignore: Ignore the value at target entirely.
actions.case_insensitive_names: Compare header names case-insensitively and ignore order across different names; the order of values within one name is kept.

rules.target: $.seatbid[*] by (seat); $.seatbid[*].bid[*] by (impid, id)
rules.justification: Go shuffles the bidder fan-out order and fills per-bidder results from map iteration, so seatbid order differs between two Go runs.
go_source: exchange/utils.go:155 for bidder, imps := range impsByBidder

rules.target: $.ext.warnings.*[*]; $.ext.errors.*[*] (exchange.response: $.ext_bid_response.warnings and errors); request.validated and privacy.labels: the entry's own warnings
rules.justification: Bidder goroutines append errors and warnings concurrently, and imp ext validation and the per-bidder privacy split append one warning per disabled, unknown or privacy-blocked bidder while ranging over a map; Go's own endpoint tests compare them order-insensitively.
go_source: ortb/request_validator.go:125 for bidder, val := range prebid.Bidder
exchange/utils.go:156 for bidder, imps := range impsByBidder

rules.target: $.ext.debug.httpcalls.*[*]
rules.justification: A bidder with several requests sends them from concurrent goroutines and collects results in completion order.

rules.target: $[*] (trace.http_out) by (kind, bidder, orig_url, sha256(request body)); drop $[*].seq
rules.justification: Outbound calls of different bidders and of one bidder with several requests run concurrently, so the global sequence number and arrival order vary between Go runs.

rules.target: stage keys bidder#call
rules.justification: MakeBids runs in response-arrival order for a bidder with several requests, so the call index is re-derived from the request each response belongs to.

rules.target: $.ext.prebid.seatnonbid[*] by (seat); $.ext.prebid.seatnonbid[*].nonbid[*] by (impid, statuscode); seat_non_bids: each seat's list $.*[*] by (impid, statuscode)
rules.justification: SeatNonBidBuilder is a map keyed by seat; its Slice() order follows map iteration.

rules.target: per-seat bid lists: bids.adjusted $.bids[*] by (imp_id, bid_id); bidder.result $.seat_bids[*].bids[*] and hooks.all_processed_bid_responses $.*.bids[*] by (bid.impid, bid.id); events.tracking $.bids.*[*] by (bid_id); bids.adjusted $.conversion_errors[*] by content (call first); bidder.result: the entry's errors and warnings by (code, message)
rules.justification: A bidder with several requests sends them from concurrent goroutines and appends each response's bids, and the errors its MakeBids returns, in completion order, so the order of one seat's bids and of the bidder's errors differs between Go runs. The final response's bids are sorted by (impid, id) already (seatbid_order).

rules.target: MakeRequests output $.requests[*] by (uri, method, imp_ids, body)
rules.justification: Adapters that group imps by a map key (matterfullrtb by publisher hash, among others) return one request per group in map iteration order. The exchange sends the requests concurrently, so their order is not observable downstream, and Go's adapter tests match requests without assuming order.
go_source: adapters/adapterstest/test_json.go:251 try to match expected to actual without assuming order

rules.target: Prebid Cache calls (kind cache): request body $.puts[*] by (type, value), with the response body $.responses[*] permuted alongside because responses[i] answers puts[i]
rules.justification: doCache builds the cache request by iterating the per-imp and per-bidder bid maps, so the order of puts (and of the returned UUIDs) differs between Go runs.
go_source: exchange/auction.go:229 for impID, topBidsPerImp := range a.allBidsByBidder
exchange/auction.go:230 for bidderName, topBidsPerBidder := range topBidsPerImp

rules.target: $.ext.responsetimemillis (exchange.response: $.ext_bid_response.responsetimemillis)
rules.justification: Values are wall-clock elapsed times of each bidder call.

rules.target: $.ext.prebid.auctiontimestamp (exchange.response: $.ext_bid_response.prebid.auctiontimestamp; events.tracking: $.auction_timestamp_ms)
rules.justification: Set from the request start time in milliseconds.

rules.target: query parameter ts= of every event URL (bid.ext.prebid.events.*, VAST impression trackers, cached VAST)
rules.justification: Event URLs carry the auction timestamp in milliseconds.

rules.target: $[*].object.start_time_set
rules.justification: AuctionObject.StartTime is time.Now() at request start; the analytics projection reports only whether it was set.

rules.target: $.id of the request and of everything derived from it, only when the input request id was {{UUID}} or generate_request_id applied
rules.justification: Go generates a random v4 UUID for the request id.

rules.target: $.source.tid and $.imp[*].ext.tid, only when absent or {{UUID}} in the input (or generate_request_id applied)
rules.justification: Go fills missing transaction ids with random v4 UUIDs.

rules.target: $.seatbid[*].bid[*].ext.prebid.bidid and every reference to it (event URLs bidid=, targeting, cache keys)
rules.justification: With generate_bid_id enabled Go assigns random v4 UUIDs to bids.

rules.target: UUIDs returned by the (mock) Prebid Cache and their references (hb_cache_id, hb_uuid, cache.bids.cacheId, cache URLs)
rules.justification: Cache keys come from the cache service response; with oracle templates they may be generated per call.

rules.target: every execution_time_millis / ExecutionTimeMillis member of hook outcomes ($.ext.prebid.modules.trace..)
rules.justification: Wall-clock duration of hook execution.

rules.target: histogram/summary series whose name ends in _time, _time_seconds, _duration or _duration_seconds, or that record request/adapter/overhead/hook/cache/stored-data timing
rules.justification: Observed values are wall-clock durations; only the number of observations is deterministic.
go_source: metrics/prometheus/prometheus.go RecordRequestTime, RecordAdapterTime, RecordOverheadTime, RecordStoredDataFetchTime, RecordPrebidCacheRequestTime, RecordModuleDuration

rules.target: series of the Go runtime collector: names starting with go_, after any configured namespace/subsystem prefix
rules.justification: The Go runtime collector reports the process's own memory, GC, scheduler and goroutine state, which changes during every case independently of the request; its runtime/metrics histograms also carry NaN sums.

rules.target: headers (semantic header comparison only)
rules.justification: Go's http.Header canonicalizes names and has no order across names; the semantic header comparison follows RFC 9110 5.1. Wire-level case and order differences are still reported as kind 'wire' (not_normalized).

rules.target: response header Date
rules.justification: net/http writes the current time into every response.

rules.target: object member order (semantic JSON comparison only)
rules.justification: JSON objects are unordered (RFC 8259); Go sorts map keys and Rust HashMap does not. The lexical comparison of raw bytes still reports member order as kind 'lexical' class 'member_order' (not_normalized).
go_source: encoding/json and jsoniter sort map keys

rules.target: trace.stages.*.*.seq
rules.justification: Session-wide sequence numbers depend on goroutine scheduling across bidders.

not_normalized.description: Differences that are never normalized and always gate parity (orchestrator decision). They are reported with their own mismatch kind and class so they can be triaged, but they count against parity/baseline.json like every other mismatch.

classes.header_case: Header name spelling on the wire differs (Go writes canonical case; HTTP/1.1 Go clients send e.g. 'Content-Type').
classes.header_order: Order of different header names on the wire differs.
classes.default_header: A client/server default header differs or is present on one side only (User-Agent Go-http-client/1.1, Accept-Encoding gzip added by Go's transport, Content-Length vs chunked).
classes.http_version: Request or response protocol version differs.
classes.content_length: Content-Length differs or is present on one side only.

classes.html_escape: Go's json.Marshal/jsoniter escape <, > and & as \u003c, \u003e, \u0026 (EscapeHTML true) except where Go disables it (endpoints/openrtb2/auction.go:384 SetEscapeHTML(false)).
classes.unicode_escape: Other string escapes differ (\u2028, \u2029, invalid UTF-8 replacement, \/).
classes.number_format: Number spelling differs (1 vs 1.0, exponent form, float formatting).
classes.trailing_newline: Encoder.Encode adds a trailing newline that json.Marshal does not (endpoints/openrtb2/auction.go:383-394).
classes.member_order: Object member order differs in the raw bytes.
classes.other: Any other byte-level difference between semantically equal JSON.

adapter_fakes.description: The 8 adapters with internal randomness or wall-clock reads get deterministic fakes (fakes.json) through branch-only seams; their outputs are compared exactly, never normalized.
